questions.text: A profitable manufacturer records €60m revenue from credit sales, but customers have not paid by year-end. Which statement is correct?

options.a: Operating cash increases automatically once a sales invoice has been issued.
options.b: Accrual profit can increase without a matching current-period cash inflow.
options.c: Both accrual profit and operating cash must increase by €60m simultaneously.
options.d: The sale should be classified as financing cash flow until customers pay.
options.e: The €60m is a direct operating inflow because a receivable is considered cash under IAS 7.
options.f: A credit sale cannot increase accrual net income until customers have made the associated cash payments.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. CFO can be presented using direct or indirect methods.
II. CFF is prepared by adjusting net income for depreciation.
III. CFI reports cash purchases and sales of long-term operating assets.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I, II and III
options.b: III only
options.c: I and III only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: A company buys a new factory for €75m cash, issues €50m long-term debt and receives €18m from customers for past invoices. How are these cash flows classified?

options.a: CFI −€75m; CFF +€50m; CFO +€18m
options.b: CFF −€75m; CFI +€50m; CFO +€18m
options.c: CFI −€75m; CFO +€50m; CFF +€18m
options.d: CFI +€75m; CFF +€50m; CFO +€18m, because acquiring PPE creates a cash inflow.

questions.text: A firm records depreciation of €30m. Under the indirect cash-flow method, assuming no other adjustments, this item is:

options.a: deducted from net income because it represents a new capital expenditure.
options.b: deducted from investing cash flow because it increases the asset's market value.
options.c: added back to net income because it reduced earnings without using current cash.
options.d: added to financing cash flow because non-cash items represent shareholder loans.

questions.text: Working-capital data show a €15m increase in trade receivables and an €8m increase in trade payables. The combined indirect-method CFO adjustment, all else equal, is:

options.a: −€23m, because both working-capital increases reduce CFO in the reconciliation.
options.b: +€23m, because both working-capital increases add to CFO in the reconciliation.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Non-cash depreciation is generally subtracted from net income to determine CFO.
II. An increase in operating payables generally increases CFO in that reconciliation.
III. An increase in operating receivables generally reduces CFO in the indirect reconciliation.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: I, II and III
options.c: II and III only
options.d: I and II only
options.e: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A company has net income of €140m, depreciation €28m, receivables increase €17m and payables decrease €9m. Ignoring other adjustments, its indirect-method CFO is:

options.e: €150m, treating the increase in receivables as a cash inflow and the decrease in payables as an inflow.
options.f: €124m, deducting depreciation and the working-capital changes from net income.

questions.text: In the direct method, cash collected from customers differs from reported sales primarily when:

options.a: the company refinances its bonds at a different coupon.
options.b: depreciation and amortization increase during the period.
options.c: the company issues shares to finance its production assets.
options.d: receivables or customer advances change during the period.

questions.text: Which cash-flow transaction is classified as financing under the convention illustrated in the lecture?

options.a: Cash paid to acquire a new manufacturing production line.
options.b: Cash received from selling a non-trading investment in bonds.
options.c: Cash collected from trade receivables arising from product sales.
options.d: Cash paid to repurchase the company's own ordinary shares.

questions.text: A firm reports CFO +€240m, CFI −€170m and CFF −€85m. What is the year's net change in cash before exchange-rate adjustments?

Consider the statements.
I. An asset disposal can produce a positive investing cash flow.
II. An increase in CFO necessarily requires an increase in net income.
III. A share repurchase can produce a negative financing cash flow.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.b: II only
options.c: I, II and III
options.d: II and III only
options.e: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A company has CFO €300m and CFI −€185m. Using the chapter's simplified definition of FCF, which pair is correct?

options.a: FCF €485m; financing cash flow is included when dividends were paid.
options.b: FCF €115m; financing cash flow is excluded from this measure.
options.c: FCF €485m; dividends are automatically included in this measure.
options.d: FCF €485m; financing cash flow is excluded from this measure.
options.e: FCF €115m; dividends are deducted twice from this measure.

questions.text: A mature company has stable positive CFO, recurring negative CFI for maintenance investment, and negative CFF from dividends and debt repayment. This pattern most closely fits:

options.a: a cash-generating mature business funding investments and shareholder/debt payouts.
options.b: a firm whose operating cash must be negative because cash used in investing is negative.
options.c: an early-stage start-up fully dependent on issuing equity to fund its losses.
options.d: a business with zero capital expenditure and rapidly increasing external financing.

questions.text: A biotech company has negative CFO, negative CFI and positive CFF funded by new equity. Which inference is most appropriate?

options.a: It may be in an early investment stage relying on outside financing for cash needs.
options.b: It is necessarily a mature company returning surplus cash to existing owners.
options.c: Raising external equity guarantees that an early-stage company will generate positive operating cash flow in the following fiscal year.
options.d: A negative CFO proves the company already has no liquidity, irrespective of existing balances and funding access.
options.e: It must report positive net income because shareholders have invested new funds.
options.f: It has already funded investment using cash proceeds from discontinued operations.

questions.text: A retailer reports CFO €90m, CFI +€140m (mostly proceeds from selling stores) and CFF −€170m. What is the key concern with interpreting its positive total cash flow?

options.a: Positive investing cash flow necessarily reflects rising expenditure on future capacity.
options.b: The sale of long-term assets must be included in operating revenue and operating CFO.
options.c: Negative financing cash flow necessarily proves the firm is in the startup phase.
options.d: Asset disposals may be non-recurring sources of cash despite weak underlying reinvestment.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Liquidity focuses on ability to meet near-term obligations.
II. Financial flexibility is identical to current-period net income.
III. Solvency concerns the capacity to meet obligations across maturities.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I, II and III
options.b: I and II only
options.c: III only
options.d: II and III only
options.e: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A company recognizes a €25m gain when selling equipment for €60m cash. In the indirect cash-flow statement, which treatment avoids double counting?

options.a: Retain the €25m equipment-sale gain within CFO and also include the full €60m cash proceeds in investing without a reconciliation.
options.b: Deduct the full €60m from CFO because the sale proceeds were never included in net income.
options.c: Deduct the full €60m from CFO and report the €25m gain in CFI.
options.d: Add the full €60m to CFO and deduct the €25m gain from CFI.
options.e: Add the gain in CFO reconciliation and report the €60m receipt in CFF.
options.f: Deduct the gain from CFO reconciliation and report the €60m receipt in CFI.

questions.text: A firm records net income of €80m but CFO of −€25m, largely from rising receivables and inventories. The most informative interpretation is:

options.a: Negative CFO proves reported revenue must be reversed under every IFRS standard.
options.b: The firm has already repaid all outstanding debt through profitable customer sales.
options.c: Positive net income automatically means its operations require no external financing.
options.d: Reported earnings have not yet translated into cash, so working-capital quality merits scrutiny.

questions.text: Which pair of cash-flow calculations can be produced without looking at financing cash flow?

options.a: CFF − CFI as the simplified free-cash-flow measure.
options.b: CFO + CFI as the simplified free-cash-flow measure.
options.c: CFO + CFF as the simplified free-cash-flow measure.
options.d: Net income + CFF as the simplified free-cash-flow measure.

questions.text: A company reports depreciation €42m, amortization €9m, pension provisions €6m and net income €95m. Under the chapter's practitioner operating-cash approximation, the result is:

Consider the statements.
I. The practitioner formula omits some working-capital movements.
II. The practitioner formula always equals IFRS CFO exactly.
III. The indirect CFO method starts from accounting income and adjusts it.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: I, II and III
options.c: I and II only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: A company's inventory purchases use €35m cash, while it receives €50m cash from new debt. Which cash-flow sections reflect these changes most directly?

options.a: CFO inflow and CFI outflow
options.b: CFI outflow and CFO inflow
options.c: Both cash flows are operating because the loan proceeds are being used for routine inventory purchases.
options.d: CFF outflow and CFI inflow
options.f: Investing outflow €35m; operating inflow €50m, because all borrowing is related to routine business operations.

questions.text: A company has positive total cash flow only because it has borrowed more than it invested. Which conclusion is unjustified?

options.a: Borrowing proceeds affect financing cash flow rather than current net income.
options.b: The cash-flow statement can identify the financing source of cash accumulation.
options.c: The company may have increased cash without improving core operating performance.
options.d: The business model has become profitable and self-financing by generating strong CFO.

questions.text: A firm uses the indirect method and reports an increase in deferred revenue of €18m. Holding other factors constant, the reconciliation to CFO generally:

options.a: deducts €18m, because prepaid customer cash has no economic value.
options.b: deducts €18m from CFF, because customer cash is new equity financing.
options.c: adds €18m, because cash arrived ahead of recognized revenue.
options.d: An increase in deferred revenue reduces current-period CFO because advance payments are not considered cash until performance occurs.
options.e: adds €18m to CFI, because unearned revenue is a long-term asset.

questions.text: Suppose operating cash flow increases from €100m to €160m because suppliers are paid substantially later, while revenue and margin remain unchanged. What interpretation is strongest?

options.a: Cash from investing activities must have increased by the same €60m.
options.b: Cash generation improved partly through payable timing, which may not be sustainable.
options.c: The extension of payment terms guarantees an equivalent sustainable margin increase.
options.d: Operating profitability must have increased by €60m under accrual accounting.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Payments to purchase PPE are investing cash outflows.
II. Proceeds from new share issues are financing cash inflows.
III. Repayment of loan principal is an operating cash outflow by definition.
Which set is correct?

options.a: II only
options.b: III only
options.c: I and III only
options.d: I and II only

questions.text: A firm sells equipment for €20m cash, purchases new PPE for €90m and receives €30m of dividends from a non-trading investment. Under the slide's investing classification for disposals and investments, which clearly belongs in CFI?

options.a: The €90m PPE purchase and new common-share proceeds.
options.b: The €20m disposal receipt and its ordinary customer collections.
options.c: The €20m disposal receipt and the €90m PPE purchase.
options.d: Only the PPE purchase belongs in investing; proceeds from asset disposals are classified in operating cash flow.
options.e: The €90m PPE purchase and its ordinary employee payroll.

questions.text: The lecture cautions that free cash flow can mislead valuation. Which reason is most important?

options.a: Current investment cash outflows may create value rather than destroy it.
options.b: Depreciation always reduces future operating cash by its book amount.
options.c: A profitable company is never required to make productive investment.
options.d: All business assets are recognized at current market value in the accounts.

questions.text: A firm reports CFO of €130m, CFI of −€180m and CFF of +€80m. Which conclusion follows?

options.a: A positive cash change proves that operating cash generation fully covered investments without any external financing.
options.b: Cash falls by €50m because financing proceeds are excluded from the cash bridge.
options.c: Cash rises by €30m although operations do not fully fund investment.
options.d: Cash falls by €30m although operations more than fund investment.
options.e: The positive cash change proves the firm has no need to refinance debt maturing in the next period.
options.f: Cash rises by €210m because financing and operating flows are positive.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. A business with positive CFO cannot have negative total cash flow.
II. A business can report accounting profit alongside negative CFO.
III. A business can show positive cash change largely from financing inflows.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: I, II and III
options.c: I and II only
options.d: II only

questions.text: A company's operating cash flow has remained positive, but capital spending repeatedly exceeds CFO. If it does not sell assets, which source is most likely needed to cover the gap?

options.a: Outside financing or existing cash reserves.
options.b: Other comprehensive income without cash receipt.
options.c: A higher reported gross margin without receipts.
options.d: Additional depreciation expense without cash receipt.

questions.text: A business receives €95m for disposing of a subsidiary and pays €35m for new equipment. Which amount contributes directly to investing cash flow, ignoring all other investing items?
A company reports €40m cash from operations but must repay €120m of maturing loans next month. Which statement best distinguishes the relevant concepts?

options.a: Positive CFO is equivalent to an interest-free commitment from all existing lenders.
options.b: Positive CFO proves solvency because contractual principal never requires cash settlement.
options.c: Positive CFO alone does not prove short-term liquidity or debt-refinancing capacity is adequate.
options.d: Positive CFO rules out liquidity stress regardless of cash balance and refinancing options.

questions.text: A firm's CFO rises from €100m to €130m, while CFI changes from −€40m to −€120m. How does simplified free cash flow change?

options.a: From +€140m to +€250m
options.b: From +€60m to +€50m
options.c: From +€60m to −€20m
options.d: From +€140m to +€10m

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. The direct method itemizes customer receipts and operating payments.
II. The indirect method adjusts for non-cash charges and changes in accruals.
III. The choice of method should change the underlying net cash generated by operations.
Which set is correct?

options.a: III only
options.b: I and II only
options.c: I and III only
options.d: None of I, II or III

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Issuing ordinary shares is normally a financing cash inflow.
II. Depreciation is an actual cash payment to the supplier each fiscal year.
III. A receipt from a bond issue is an investing cash inflow.
Which set is correct?

options.a: III only
options.b: II only
options.c: I and II only
options.d: I and III only

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Financing inflows can temporarily mask weak operating cash generation.
II. A firm can be profitable and still be short of cash.
III. Cash from investing is often negative when productive assets are purchased.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I, II and III
options.b: II and III only
options.c: III only
options.d: I and III only
